gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on the 5-port UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W (X774) only USB-C1 and USB-C2 are the PD 3.1 140 W ports (C3 is PD 3.0 at 100 W, C4 30 W), or that Apple's 140 W adapter sold since 2026-10-28 has the pill-shaped AC Connector 2, whose plugs Apple says are not cross-compatible with the older connector type.
standout_why: Compared against thegadgetmasters.com (cited), Macworld (cited), Apple Support 102378 (cited), thisUSB, SpecSource, CompatWiki and MacRumors 2026-04-02. The core of this angle, the cable by model-year matrix (MagSafe 3 for every 2021-or-later 16-inch, 240 W USB-C cable for Nov 2023 or later), is already in Apple's page, thisUSB, thegadgetmasters and ChatGPT's own answer. What they lack is small: Macworld describes the 4-port Nexode Pro 160W (140/100/30/22.5 W) and thegadgetmasters the retractable-cable one, so neither maps the 5-port X774's ports; SpecSource lists X774 only as '140W single-port max'. MacRumors' April page reports the plug mismatch, but not the 2026-10-28 replacement parts or Apple's cross-compatibility sentence. I could not open UGREEN's own page (HTTP 403/429), so the X774 port map rests on Notebookcheck, not the maker's table.
decides: It confirms the pick and does not change it. The page should name the port for the UGREEN 5-port (USB-C1 or USB-C2, not C3) and name the cable by Mac year: the USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable from the Mac's box gives 140 W on every 2021-or-later 16-inch, while a USB-C to USB-C cable does so only on Nov 2023-or-later models and only if 240 W-rated. On the Apple row, add that the current adapter's AC Connector 2 does not take the older extension cable or travel plugs. Follow Apple, not Macworld, on the Nov 2023 (M3 Pro/Max) model: Apple lists it for the 240 W USB-C cable, Macworld says models older than M4 must use MagSafe 3.

findings.label: Apple's fast-charge pairings for the 16-inch MacBook Pro (2021 or later)
findings.value: 140W USB-C Power Adapter with a USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable; or 140W USB-C Power Adapter with the 240W USB-C Charge Cable for MacBook Pro (16-inch, Nov 2023) or later; or Apple Studio Display XDR with a Thunderbolt cable. Up to 50% in about 30 minutes.
findings.source_title: Fast charge your MacBook Air or MacBook Pro - Apple Support
findings.note: Page dated 2026-11-05. Unlike the 14-inch list, the 16-inch list has no 96 W adapter and no third-party display option. Apple names only its own adapter here and does not say which Mac port to use.

findings.label: Apple's wording on third-party power sources, and what ships in the 16-inch box (M5 Pro / M5 Max)
findings.value: "Fast-charge capable with 140W or higher USB PD power source"; minimum wattage recommended to charge: 94W; in the box: 140W USB-C Power Adapter and USB-C to MagSafe 3 Cable (2 m); ports: three Thunderbolt 5 (USB-C) with charging, plus MagSafe 3
findings.note: Apple's spec page accepts any USB PD source of 140 W or higher, not only its own adapter. The MagSafe 3 cable every 16-inch owner already has is the one cable that covers all model years. thegadgetmasters already quotes the 94 W / 140 W lines, so this is not new against rivals.
